pr_body:
This PR adds some timeouts to keyring operations that have been reported as hanging in some WSL and Windows machines. The underlying issue stems from the `go-keyring` package that we use so until the bugs get fixed there we should properly handle the cases where it hangs. 

Fixes https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/7208

issue_context.title: gh repo command is slower in wsl2
issue_context.body:
### GitHub CLI command "gh repo create" slow to respond in wsl2 

gh version 2.24.3

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Type this 'gh repo create '
2. View the output ' interactive menu do not appear (some time takes up 10 min)'

### Expected vs actual behavior
Expected behavior : interactive menu should appear as soon as command is pressed
Actual Behavior : it takes upto 10 min to open interactive menu 
While it is not working on wsl2 but it is working perfectly on windows command prompt 
### Logs

Paste the activity from your command line. Redact if needed.
comments: @VikasPoddar Sorry you are having this trouble. We have not had reports in the past of `gh` being slow inside wsl2. Are you seeing slowness for commands that do not have interactive prompts? Did this issue start recently?
I use gh on wsl2 daily and can't reproduce this, FWIW. ran in both Alacritty and Windows Terminal.

> gh repo list

But no problem are occurring in powershell environment.
I have reinstalled gh CLI but this condition occured again

@VikasPoddar As the team has not been able to reproduce this issue I am not sure there is much else we can do to help without more information to go on. The only idea I have left is to update `gh` to the latest version as there were a couple bug fixes since version 2.24.3.

@samcoe Okay sir, I will reinstall the gh CLI tool
And will inform you

By default, dbus (which gh tries to use to communicate to Secret Service on linux) is not running under WSL2, and an attempt to retrieve an encrypted token should immediately fail and the lookup should fall back to gh's config file instead.

However, for you and apparently for @mbates and some other users the operation seems to hang for a long time or indefinitely. I'm not sure what circumstances lead to this, but @vilmibm was guessing that this might be affecting users who have taken steps to explicitly enable dbus in their WSL2 instances. Does this describe you?

In any case, I'm considering adding some debugging to token lookups so that the user at least gets an indication where the gh process is stuck.
@benjlevesque I will take a look at it. Thank you

review_comments:
I'm trying to figure out if this function is racy or not. See this playground: https://go.dev/play/p/hCpEywlYjiR which you can run a few times to see different results).

I **think** it is racy, like the example in the playground, but I can't quite convince myself that `time.Sleep` doesn't have some impact on goroutine scheduling. Either way, unless you're sure this code isn't racy then I think we should change it. At the heart of the issue is that `select` can choose any channel branch that succeeds, and putting a value on one channel can race with closing the other, e.g. `errCh <- err` racing with `close(resCh)`.

There are a few possible (I think) fixes for this:
 1. Using unbuffered channels will block the write until someone reads, preventing the `close` until a branch has already been picked
 2. Move the `closes` until after a decision has been made
 3. Use a result struct `type result struct { secret string, error string }` or anonymous struct `c := make(chan struct { string; error })` and only have a single channel
 
I would favour 3, as any use of multiple channels has the propensity to introduce these kinds of hard to reason about issues and there's probably a reason I've seen it used so many times.

On the other hand, if you know a reason this isn't racy then please hit me with that knowledge!

Great catch here, I do think there is a race condition! I had not thought about how `select` would work with `defer close`. I was thinking about using option 3 originally, seems like the best solution, I will make the change.
